problem: Robot foundation models and VLAs focus on physical task competence. They do not handle socially intelligent interaction: understanding shifting user intent, asking clarifying questions, and revising an action already underway when the user corrects or interrupts mid-task. Doing this requires speech, perception, memory, navigation and manipulation to work as one integrated real-time system.
motivation: Natural human–robot collaboration needs the robot to interpret intent, talk naturally and adapt ongoing behavior as new information arrives. The paper's example is a user switching from Coke to Pepsi while the robot is already reaching. Coordinating specialized capabilities over time and revising them mid-execution motivates an agentic architecture rather than a single end-to-end model. Existing VLM benchmarks score isolated predictions, not sustained closed-loop interaction.
key_idea: A fine-tuned open VLM (Qwen3.5), trained on synthetic multi-turn tool-call traces full of ambiguity, corrections and interruptions, acts as the reasoning core. At each step it picks exactly one tool (speak, look up keypoints, navigate, check reachability, run a GR00T VLA, wait). A real-time harness executes the tools, manages context and asynchronous speech, and lets new user input redirect ongoing actions on a Unitree G1 humanoid.
insight: Supervised fine-tuning on synthetic interaction traces substantially improves closed-loop agent competence at the same model size: on the Interaction Core28 closed-loop benchmark, 4B goes from 10/28 to 17/28 and 9B from 11/28 to 20/28. The fine-tuned 9B approaches a frontier model with an optimized prompt (GPT-5.6 with GEPA, 26/28). The synthetic traces have tool-call correctness guaranteed by construction (state machine + policy table), and an LLM teacher only writes the language. Keeping metric planning and motor control outside the VLM makes the interface simple: named keypoints for navigation, a reachability gate before picking, and a VLA registry that exposes new skills without retraining the agent. Remaining failures concentrate in spatial grounding of the hand-off location at delivery. Latency matters enough that the smaller 4B model was deployed despite its lower success.
method: Reasoning core VLM: Qwen3.5 (4B deployed, 9B also trained) fine-tuned with LoRA via SFT. Inputs are the ego-view image, four panoramic views from a head-mounted 360° camera, transcribed speech, and interaction history including its own reasoning and prior tool results. It outputs reasoning plus a single typed function call.

Fixed tool set with typed schemas: say, lookup_keypoints (static map of named rooms/locations sorted by distance), navigate (to a named keypoint), reachability (whether a visible object is pickable and with which arm), vla (pick/place via a trained VLA policy), wait. The harness enforces at most one action-bearing call per turn, requires a successful reachability check immediately before a pick, and rejects malformed calls. The object_type vocabulary is read at runtime from the VLA registry.

Synthetic training corpus: 14,432 multi-turn trajectories generated combinatorially over tasks, objects and interaction events. A state machine and policy table fix tool calls, arguments and results. A teacher LLM writes reasoning, speech and user utterances, filtered by rule-based checks and a two-stage LLM judge with up to two revision attempts. Imagery comes from generated images and simulator renders mirroring the deployment space.

Real-time harness: assembles context, calls the VLM, validates and executes the tool, then loops. Speech transcripts trigger new turns. Speech output is asynchronous via a FIFO audio queue. An auxiliary model compacts context non-blockingly, installed only between turns. Visual prefill refreshes the camera input before instructions arrive. Local sherpa-onnx STT averages 94.7 ms per 10 s clip. New user input can interrupt navigation or manipulation.

Humanoid navigation: KISS-ICP LiDAR odometry plus an EKF (Optuna-tuned) for localization, navigation to named semantic keypoints, and an orientation-aware continuous planner for fine motion. The planner uses quintic splines with heading decoupled from travel direction and a multi-circle footprint for turning, strafing and narrow passages.

Manipulation: GR00T N1.7 VLA initialized from the pretrained UNITREE_G1 embodiment and fine-tuned on real-robot teleoperation pick-and-place demos. It controls arm and gripper only (Dex-3 hand) and predicts 30-step action chunks at 30 Hz. A calibrated Isaac Sim G1 model (camera mask IoU ~0.92, hand tracking error 0.043 rad) is used only to screen policies.

Closed-loop evaluation: Interaction Core28 in AI2-THOR/ProcTHOR homes fixed by hash. It uses the same tool interface, system prompt and four-view camera geometry as the robot, with a scripted simulated user. Success requires clean termination, passing deterministic interaction gates, and reaching the correct final simulator state. An LLM judge may overturn only failures that come solely from the semantic content of an utterance.

setting.backbone: Qwen3.5-4B VLM fine-tuned with LoRA (deployed); Qwen3.5-9B also fine-tuned. GR00T N1.7 VLA (fine-tuned) for manipulation; classical LiDAR localization and spline planner for navigation.
setting.training_data: 14,432 fully synthetic multi-turn tool-call trajectories: language written by a teacher LLM, images generated or rendered from simulated environments mirroring the deployment space. VLA fine-tuned on real-robot G1 teleoperation pick-and-place demos (count not given).
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB ego-view plus four panoramic views from a head-mounted 360° camera, transcribed user speech, interaction history and tool results. LiDAR for localization in the navigation stack.
setting.action_space: High-level single tool call per step (say / lookup_keypoints / navigate to named keypoint / reachability / vla / wait). Navigation executed by keypoint navigation plus a continuous quintic-spline planner. Manipulation executed as 30-step arm/gripper action chunks at 30 Hz.
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR with ProcTHOR homes (agent evaluation); Isaac Sim (VLA development/screening); real Unitree G1 deployment
setting.privileged: Pre-built static map of named semantic keypoints (rooms/desks/tables) and LiDAR-based localization; navigation only to named keypoints

numbers_note: The only quantitative agent result is the 28-scenario in-house Core28 benchmark, reported as success counts rather than percentages. There is no standard navigation benchmark, and real-robot results are demonstrations only. Other numbers are component measurements, not benchmark results: STT latency 94.7 ms mean / 99.2 ms P95, Isaac Sim camera mask IoU ~0.92, Dex-3 tracking error 0.132 → 0.043 rad. The GPT-5.6 (GEPA-optimized prompt) 26/28 row is a baseline and is excluded.
results: On the closed-loop Interaction Core28 benchmark (AI2-THOR/ProcTHOR, 28 scenarios), fine-tuning roughly doubles success at both sizes: Qwen3.5-4B goes from 10/28 to 17/28 and 9B from 11/28 to 20/28. The fine-tuned 9B approaches GPT-5.6 with a GEPA-optimized prompt (26/28) but does not beat it. The 4B model is deployed on a real Unitree G1 for latency reasons. Qualitatively, the system handles mid-task intent changes in a real-robot demo: it abandons a Coke reach, picks the Pepsi, navigates to the bedroom and delivers it.
limitations: Integration is operational, not learned: speech, memory, navigation and manipulation are separate modules coordinated through tool calls. This can cause context loss, latency, brittle handoffs and fragmented behavior, and there is no unified representation of user, environment and robot state.

Evaluation is small and in-house: 28 scripted scenarios with a scripted user and synthetic training data. There is no quantitative real-robot evaluation and no standard navigation benchmark. Navigation relies on a pre-built static map of named keypoints. The fine-tuned models still trail a frontier prompted model, and failures concentrate in spatial grounding of hand-off locations.
Fine-tuned VLA manipulation skills are limited to the target home's pick-and-place tasks. Sim-to-real policy rankings were not preserved, so real-robot validation is still required.
